backgrounds.name: the river of a spinning hole
backgrounds.description: The river of space round a black hole of 4 million solar masses spinning at 0.9 of the most it can, in its equatorial plane (Hamilton and Lisle's river model, in Doran's coordinates). The river (grey arrows) flows straight in, with no swirl, at c sqrt(2GM/c^2 r), where r = sqrt(R^2 - a^2) and R is the distance from the hole; g (dark arrows) is its acceleration. The colour map is the river's twist: how far it turns anything carried in it about the spin axis, in radians, largest close in. The twist arcs are how fast the twist changes along the way in: the rate, in radians a second, at which it turns something moving straight in through the river at c; each arc turns the way that thing is turned. The paths round a hole with no spin are drawn against the same background.
